newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia sees no quick mandate for Russian troops.
newsitem.headline: Georgia sees no quick mandate for Russian troops.

text.p: Georgia's foreign minister said on Wednesday his country had no intention of renewing a mandate for Russian peacekeepers in a buffer zone between Georgia and its separatist province of Abkhazia but added that Tbilisi was not insisting on their quick withdrawal.

"It is our opinion that we should not extend the mandate of the Russian peacekeeping force," Irakly Menagarishvili told national radio. "At the same time, that does not mean we are raising the question of the withdrawal of the peacekeepers."
Observers fear the renewal of the bloody 1992-93 conflict between Georgians and Abkhazians in which thousands of people were killed if the 1,500-strong force is withdrawn.

A senior Russian foreign ministry official said earlier on Wednesday the force would be pulled out after its mandate expried unless Tbilisi formally requested an extension. But he said President Boris Yeltsin had the last word on the question.

Menagarishvili repeated Georgia's demand that the Russian force take on additional responsibilities - policing more of Abkhazia and helping to resettle Georgian refugees - for the renewal of the mandate.

But he repeated President Eduard Shevardnadze's statement earlier this week that the question of the peacekeepers was a delicate one and that Tbilisi was not insisting on their withdrawal. Shevardnadze said the future of the force should be decided by the Commonwealth of former Soviet republics in September.
